q: What does this red octagonal sign require?
o: Come to a full stop, then go only when the way is clear
Come to a full stop only if cross traffic is approaching
Slow down, and stop only if the way is not clear
Come to a full stop; cross traffic must then yield to you
ex: The red octagon is a STOP sign. Come to a full stop and proceed only when you are sure the way is clear.

q: Which type of sign uses this white rectangular shape?
o: Regulatory: it states the law (speed, parking, turns)
ex: White rectangles or squares are regulatory signs. They state the law, such as speed limits, parking rules, and turning and passing movements.

o: Slow down, give the right of way, and stop if necessary
Slow down; you have the right of way over side traffic
Always come to a full stop, then give the right of way
Give the right of way to pedestrians only, not to vehicles
ex: A triangle with a red border is a Yield sign. Slow down approaching the intersection, give the right of way, and stop if other traffic is in or closely approaching the intersection.

q: What does a yellow diamond-shaped sign tell you?
o: Dangerous or unusual conditions ahead, such as a curve or dip
A law you must obey, such as a speed limit or parking rule
Construction or maintenance work ahead on the roadway
Directional guidance, such as permitted turns or routes
ex: Warning signs are diamond shaped, yellow or orange with black letters or symbols. They warn of dangerous or unusual conditions ahead, such as a curve, turn, dip or side road.

o: Railway crossing: same as yield — give the right of way, stop if necessary
Railway crossing: same as stop — always come to a full stop
Railway ahead: the road crosses the tracks at the angle shown
Railway crossing: slow down only if the lights are flashing
ex: The crossbuck marks a railway crossing. The handbook says it has the same colour and meaning as a yield sign: give the right of way and stop if necessary.

o: School zone: obey the speed on the tab during school days
School crosswalk ahead: stop for children at the crossing
Playground zone: obey the speed on the tab at all times
School zone: the speed on the tab is a recommended speed
ex: A pentagon with a fluorescent yellow-green background and children's silhouettes is a school zone sign. The tab underneath gives the speed to observe.

o: Two lanes in your direction: pass on the left
Divided highway: keep right of the median
ex: Traffic travels in both directions on this road.

o: Maximum speed 100 km/h under ideal conditions
Minimum speed 100 km/h on this highway
Recommended speed 100 km/h (not a legal limit)
Required speed 100 km/h when traffic is light
ex: The maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions. In bad weather you should drive slower.

o: A lower maximum speed zone (50 km/h) is ahead
The 50 km/h zone starts right at this sign
A minimum speed of 50 km/h applies ahead
50 km/h applies only to straight-through traffic
ex: The arrow above the number is an advance warning: a lower maximum speed zone is ahead.

o: Turn right only at the next intersection
Lane shifts to the right ahead
ex: All traffic moves in the direction of the arrow.

q: What does this sign mean in a work zone?
o: Fines triple for speeding past workers in this work zone
Fines triple for any speeding in the zone, workers or not
Maximum 60 km/h; fines triple on weekdays only
Minimum speed 60 km/h through the work zone
ex: Maximum speed in a work zone. The speeding fine triples when you exceed the posted limit past workers (anyone within 3 km of a traffic control person, survey crew or highway workers sign).

o: Keep to the right of the traffic island or obstruction
Keep to the left of the traffic island or obstruction
Road curves right around an obstruction ahead
ex: A black shield on the left and an arrow passing it on the right: keep to the right of the traffic island or obstruction.
A red circle with a white bar means Do not enter.
A green square with a white D marks a route for over dimensional vehicles.

o: Two lanes: keep a safe following distance
ex: Two cars in a green circle: passing is allowed. The same symbol in a crossed-out red circle prohibits passing.
A red crossed-out circle with two cars means passing is not permitted. The same symbol in a green circle means passing is permitted.
A U-turn arrow in a green circle means you may turn around here.
No U-turn: you must not turn your vehicle around on the roadway to travel in the opposite direction.

o: Heavy trucks should use this roadway
No heavy trucks on this roadway
Trucks entering from a side road
ex: A truck in a green circle: heavy trucks should use this roadway.

o: No heavy trucks on this roadway
Heavy trucks should use this roadway
ex: A truck in a crossed-out red circle: heavy trucks are not allowed on this roadway.

o: Hazard close to the edge of the road
ex: A black diamond in a green circle marks the route that dangerous goods carriers should use.
The black diamond stands for dangerous goods. In a green circle it marks a dangerous goods route; in a crossed-out red circle, dangerous goods carriers are prohibited.

q: What does this sign tell you?
o: Weight limit for the highway or bridge, in tonnes
Length limit: vehicles over 10 m prohibited
Maximum speed 10 km/h on the bridge
Truck lane for vehicles over 10 tonnes
ex: The “t” stands for tonnes. This is the vehicle weight limit permitted on the highway or bridge.
A truck and a scale: a truck inspection station is here.

o: Truck inspection station exit (arrow shows the side)
Truck inspection station closed (arrow shows detour)
ex: The arrow shows which side of the road the truck inspection station exit is on.

o: Parking allowed 30 min, 9:00–18:00, Mon–Sat, as indicated
Parking allowed 30 min, Sundays only, as indicated
Pay parking 9:00–18:00, 30 min minimum, as indicated
ex: A green P: parking is allowed for the time, hours and days shown, in the direction of the arrows.

o: Do not stop to wait here at any time
No parking, but stopping briefly to wait is allowed
No stopping during rush hour only
Stop here only to let passengers out
ex: Do not stop to wait here at any time.
A crossed-out P in a red circle means parking is prohibited in the direction of the arrows.

o: Do not enter between the arrows
ex: A crossed-out stop symbol: stopping is prohibited in the direction of the arrows.
The new-style pedestrian crosswalk sign. The old style shows the word PEDESTRIAN and an X.
The old-style pedestrian crosswalk sign. The new style shows a walking figure.
The new-style school crosswalk sign with two children. The old style shows the word SCHOOL and an X.
The old-style school crosswalk sign. The new style shows two children.

q: What must traffic do at this pedestrian crosswalk?
o: Stop when the lights are flashing, then proceed when safe
Stop when the lights are flashing and wait until they go off
Slow down when the lights flash; stop only if someone is on the road
Stop only when the lights are steady, not flashing
ex: At a crosswalk with flashing lights, traffic must stop while the lights are flashing and proceed when it is safe.

o: Bus lane during the times shown
Bus lane at all times; times show bus frequency
Carpool lane during the times shown
Bus stop: no parking during the times shown
ex: A diamond with a bus symbol marks a bus lane. The times and days show when the restriction applies.
This lane is reserved for bicycles.

o: No left turn from this lane
ex: Overhead lane sign: traffic in this lane must turn left. Each overhead sign is centred over the lane it controls.
From this lane you may turn left or go straight.

q: What does this overhead sign mean?
o: Two lanes ahead merge to the left
ex: Two left arrows mean two left-turning lanes. Each overhead sign is centred over the lane it controls.

o: Two lanes ahead curve to the right
ex: Two right arrows: two lanes turn right. From the outside (left) lane you may also turn right on red after stopping and yielding.
From this lane you may turn left or right, but not go straight.
From this lane you may turn left, go straight or turn right.
Traffic in this lane must go straight through.

o: Right turn on red permitted from this lane
ex: Traffic in this lane must turn right.
From this lane you may turn right or go straight.

o: No left turn on red only
ex: A left arrow in a crossed-out red circle. A tab underneath may show hours when it applies.

o: No right turn on red only
ex: A right arrow in a crossed-out red circle. A tab underneath may show hours when it applies.

o: Go straight or turn right only
Go straight or turn left only
ex: A green circle shows the permitted movements: straight or right.

o: Go straight or turn left only
Go straight or turn right only
ex: A green circle shows permitted movements: straight through or a left turn only.

o: Turn right or left only (no straight through)
Go straight or turn either way
Road splits: keep left or right
ex: You must turn right or left; going straight is not permitted.
You must go straight; turns are not permitted.

o: Go straight or turn left only
ex: You must turn left.

o: Go straight or turn right only
ex: You must turn right.

o: No right turn on red: wait for the green light
Right turn on red allowed after a full stop
No right turn at any time
Right turn on red only when no pedestrians are present
ex: A crossed-out right arrow next to a red light: no right turn on red. Wait for the green light.

o: Centre lane for left turns from both directions
Centre lane for passing in both directions
Centre lane for left turns from your direction only
Two-way traffic: keep out of the centre lane
ex: The centre lane is used by traffic from both directions to make left turns.

o: Bicycle lane: turning vehicles may drive in it
Bicycle lane ends: bikes merge with traffic
ex: Turning vehicles must yield to cyclists travelling straight in their lane.
Ahead, the road changes to traffic in both directions.
You are approaching a divided highway.
The road surface becomes slippery when wet.
There is a bump or rough road ahead. Slow down.

o: Keep to the right of the obstruction
ex: There is an obstruction ahead. You may pass on either side.

o: Divided highway begins: keep to the right
Divided highway ends: keep to the right
ex: Arrows splitting around a median: a divided highway begins. Keep to the right.

o: Section of roadway regularly crossed by deer
Deer crossing at dusk and dawn only
ex: This section of roadway is regularly crossed by deer.

o: Steep hill ahead: shift to a lower gear or slow down
Steep hill ahead: shift to a higher gear
Steep hill ahead: applies to trucks only
Truck tipping hazard on a curve ahead
ex: Steep hill ahead. On a very steep downgrade, shift to a lower gear or slow down.
Speed on this road is photo enforced. A current list of locations is at sgi.sk.ca/photo-speed-enforcement.

o: Speed limit enforced by police patrol only
ex: Speed on this road is photo enforced. A current list of locations is at sgi.sk.ca/photo-speed-enforcement.

o: Stop sign ahead for oncoming traffic only
ex: There is a stop sign ahead. Be ready to stop.
The divided highway ends; traffic in both directions will share the road.

o: Traffic signals ahead: be prepared to stop
Pedestrian signal ahead: stop only if flashing
ex: There are traffic signals ahead. Be prepared to stop.

o: Railway ahead: tracks cross the road at the angle shown
Railway runs alongside the road; no crossing
ex: A yellow diamond with rails means a railway is ahead, crossing the road at the angle shown. The crossing itself is marked with a crossbuck.

o: Road narrows: the road ahead is not as wide
Narrow bridge ahead: the bridge is a single lane
Lane ends ahead: merge to the left
Divided highway ends: two-way traffic ahead
ex: The road ahead is not as wide as the road you are driving on.
The width of the pavement on the bridge is narrower than the approach.

o: Lane ends: the right lane ends
Lane ends: the left lane ends
ex: The right lane ends, so you will need to merge.

o: Winding road ahead, first curve to the right
Winding road ahead, first curve to the left
Reverse curve ahead, first turn right
Sharp curve to the right ahead
ex: A winding road is ahead; the first curve is to the right.

o: Reverse curve: two turns, first to the right
Reverse curve: two turns, first to the left
Winding road: three or more curves
Lane shift to the right ahead
ex: Reverse curve: two turns in opposite directions separated by less than 120 m, first turn right. A winding road sign means three or more curves.

o: Sharp curve to the right ahead
Lane shift to the right ahead
ex: There is a curve to the right ahead.

o: Sharp curve right; 30 km/h is the recommended safe speed
Sharp curve right; 30 km/h is the legal maximum
ex: A sharp curve to the right is ahead. The tab shows the recommended safe speed.
An underpass is ahead. The overhead clearance is as shown.
A road joins from the right and/or left at a hidden intersection ahead.

o: Added lane: roads converge, no merging needed
Traffic entering from the right must yield
ex: Two roads converge, and merging movements are not required.

o: Two lanes merge: traffic entering from the right
Added lane: two roads converge, no merging needed
Lane ends: the left lane ends ahead
Divided highway ends: two-way traffic ahead
ex: Traffic entering from the right merges into your lane.

o: Hazard close to the edge of the road
ex: The checkerboard diamond means the road ends.

o: Pavement drop-off: the shoulder is lower than the lane
Road ends: the road does not continue
Grooved pavement ahead: steering may feel loose
ex: The pavement ends; the road continues with a gravel surface.

o: Surface may be slippery at 0 °C: slow down
Road slippery when wet: slow down
ex: The bridge or roadway surface may be slippery at zero degrees Celsius. Slow down.

o: Snowmobile trail runs beside the road
ex: Snowmobiles cross the road ahead.
Cattle cross the road ahead.

o: T-intersection: road turns sharply right and left
Four-way intersection: roads join from all sides
Road ends: no turns are possible
Sharp curve to the right: slow down
ex: The road ends ahead at a T-intersection and turns sharply right and left.
A playground is ahead. With a km/h tab underneath, that speed must be observed.

o: Pedestrian crosswalk here: stop for pedestrians
ex: A pedestrian crosswalk or corridor is ahead.
A school bus stop is ahead. Stop for a bus with flashing lights.

q: What is the purpose of this sign?
o: Chevrons guide drivers around a sharp curve
Keep to the right of the obstruction
ex: Chevron (arrowhead) signs are posted in groups to guide drivers around sharp curves.
A school crosswalk is ahead. Fluorescent yellow-green is used for school zone and school crosswalk ahead signs.

q: What does this sign mean when you see it on the back of a vehicle?
o: Slow moving vehicle (under 40 km/h): slow down
ex: The orange triangle with a red border is mounted on the rear of vehicles travelling under 40 km/h. Slow down when approaching from behind.

o: Hazard at the road edge: pass on the side the lines slope down to
Hazard at the road edge: pass on the side the lines slope up to
ex: Marks a hazard close to the edge of the road. The downward lines show the side on which you may safely pass.
This sign is placed on over-dimension loads or on escort vehicles.

o: Traffic control person ahead: be prepared to stop
Survey crew ahead: be prepared to slow down
Highway workers present: slow to 60 km/h
School crossing guard ahead: stop for children
ex: An orange sign with a figure holding a STOP/SLOW paddle: a traffic control person (flagperson) is ahead. Be prepared to stop for instructions. This sign also marks the start of a work zone.
A survey crew is working ahead. This sign marks the start of a work zone.
Highway workers ahead; it may have a WORKERS PRESENT tab. Slow to 60 km/h or less when passing a worker.

o: Truck entrance: trucks entering, leaving or crossing
Truck inspection station: trucks must exit here
Heavy trucks should use this roadway from here on
Truck lane ends: trucks merge to the left
ex: Marks where trucks are entering, leaving or crossing the road.

q: Who must be prepared to stop at this sign?
o: Be prepared to stop if your vehicle has a high load
Low underpass ahead: all vehicles be prepared to stop
Power lines down: all traffic must stop
Overhead signs ahead: watch for lane changes
ex: The orange OVERHEAD LINES sign: be prepared to stop if you are driving a vehicle with a high load.

o: Construction ahead: be ready for speed limit changes
Construction zone ends: resume the normal speed
Detour ahead: follow the orange signs
Road closed ahead: local traffic only
ex: You are entering a construction zone. Drive with extra caution and be prepared for changes in the speed limit.
Traffic ahead may be stopped in the construction zone. Be prepared to stop.

o: Pavement drop-off: lane or shoulder is higher or lower
Pavement ends: a gravel surface continues
Steep hill ahead: shift to a lower gear
Grooved pavement ahead: steering may feel loose
ex: The adjacent lane or shoulder (or both) is lower or higher than your travel lane.
The pavement ahead is grooved, which can affect steering.

q: At a crossing without gates, the red lights are flashing and no train is close. What may you do?
o: Cross after stopping, if it is safe
Cross without stopping if no train is in sight
Wait until the lights stop flashing
Cross only if a signal person waves you through
ex: At crossings without gates you may cross after stopping while the red lights flash, if it is safe. If a train is closely approaching or a signal person tells you to stop, you must wait. Never drive around lowered gates.

q: Three triangular delineators on a stop sign post mean the crossing road is...
o: A provincial highway, grid road or major street
A main farm access road or all-weather road
A minor rural road or local street
ex: Three delineators: provincial and public highways, community access roads, grid roads, major streets. Two: main farm access roads, improved all-weather roads, intermediate urban streets. One: all other minor rural roads and local streets.
The green maple-leaf marker identifies the Trans Canada Highway.
The blue shield marks a numbered provincial highway.
The green sheaf marker identifies a numbered rural municipal route.

o: Airport: the plane points toward the airport
Airport: the plane shows the runway direction
ex: The plane points in the direction of the airport.

o: Advance community sign with service tabs
Town limits: lower speed starts here
ex: Announces a community ahead and the services available there.
A telephone is available.
Picnic facilities are available.
Accommodation is available.
Facilities for trailers are available.
Food is available.
A swimming area is available.
Camping is available.
A hospital is nearby.
A golf course is nearby.
Police services are nearby.
A museum is nearby.
Gasoline fuel is available. A D on the sign means diesel fuel.
